description: Four false findings from matching argument POSITIONS without knowing the construction. `createCipheriv(alg, key, iv)` holds an initialisation vector in the third slot in every mode that has one and holds nothing in ECB, which has none -- Node still requires the argument and an empty string is the ordinary way to write it -- so reading the third argument without the first judges an argument whose meaning has not been established. An NTLM implementation's `createCipheriv("DES-ECB", key, "")` was reported as a predictable IV on a line whose real weakness, single-DES in ECB, was already being reported correctly one rule over: the finding was pure duplication of a true statement plus a false one. The mode test is written as a VETO on ECB and not as a list of the modes that take an IV, which `/store-configured` is the proof of: an algorithm that is a configuration value cannot be read, the IV is still written down, and trading four false findings for an unknown number of silences is not a precision fix. The same mistake lives in the other construction and the last two routes hold it: `createHmac("md5", key)` is not `createHash("md5")`, because what makes an HMAC sound is the key rather than the hash's collision resistance and HMAC-MD5 has no practical forgery -- while an unkeyed MD5 handed to a verification call is the program saying in its own code that a digest is standing in for what it was computed from.

expected.note: the true statement about the NTLM line, made by a rule that reads argument ZERO. It was always being emitted; the IV finding beside it was the duplication
CBC takes an IV and this one is written down, so it is both predictable and the same for every message. The rule must not have been weakened into silence
the algorithm cannot be read and the IV can. An argument nobody wrote down disqualifies nothing -- this is what the veto's defeasibility buys
ECB is the finding wherever it appears, and this line proves the IV rule stays silent on it even when the third argument is spelled `null` rather than empty

the contrast that makes the HMAC negative a judgement rather than an exemption: an unkeyed digest handed to a verification call is being trusted to stand in for its input, which is the one job that needs collision resistance
